paragraphs: Mentioned in [Shabbat 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.22a.2), disputing with Rav Acha, son of Rava. Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Yirmiyah of Difta; he says the name became Shmuel through an error prompted by the word mi-smol, “on the left.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The heading remains Shmuel of Difta. Hyman attributes Yirmiyah of Difta to דק״ס, conventionally Dikdukei Soferim, and explains Shmuel as a corruption prompted by משמאל, mi-smol, “on the left.” The mechanism is his textual explanation, not an independently established reading history.

In the linked passage, Shmuel of Difta says to place the lamp on the left, and Rav Acha son of Rava says to place it on the right. See also [Heilprin’s notice of the same dispute](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3389&lang=en).
